blocks.html: Cells contain structures with different functions. The nucleus, chromosomes, cell membrane, mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum and ribosomes are the focus of this lesson.
We’ll see how these structures relate to movement into and out of cells, protein production, cell activities and energy transfer into ATP.
1.1 recognise cell structures as seen with a light microscope and electron microscope
(TEM images only), including nucleus, chromosomes, cell membrane, mitochondria,
endoplasmic reticulum and ribosomes
1.2 describe the functions of the cell structures:
• nucleus
• chromosomes
• cell membrane
• mitochondria
• endoplasmic reticulum
• ribosomes.

units.title: Cells
units.subtitle: THE BASIC UNITS OF LIVING ORGANISMS

blocks.html: Cells are the basic units of living organisms.
Organelles are structures inside cells with specific functions.
The structures inside a cell have different roles. Their functions form the relationships in the learning map.
The cytoplasm is jelly-like material outside the nucleus.
It contains organelles.
The cytoplasm is the site of many chemical reactions, including anaerobic respiration.

units.title: Cell membrane
units.subtitle: MOVEMENT INTO AND OUT OF THE CELL

blocks.html: The cell surface membrane controls movement into and out of the cell. This brings its boundary and its function together.
The cell surface membrane is a partially permeable boundary.
The cell surface membrane controls movement into and out of the cell.

nodes: Movement into and out of the cell

blocks.html: Substances cross by diffusion or through transport proteins.

links: cross by diffusion or through transport proteins

blocks.html: Active transport requires energy.
More of the movement of substances into and out of cells is covered in Unit 2 — Movement of substances into and out of cells.
The nucleus contains chromosomes. Chromosomes contain DNA.
Genes are sections of DNA that code for proteins.
Which genes are “switched on” determines which proteins are produced.
The proteins produced are therefore linked to which genes are switched on.
Some proteins are enzymes.
Which enzymes are produced determines which chemical reactions can occur.
The chemical reactions determine the activity of the cell.
Thus, the nucleus controls cell activities by controlling which proteins are made.

units.title: Nucleus
units.subtitle: THE RELATIONSHIP FROM GENES TO ACTIVITY

blocks.html: Which genes are switched on determines which proteins are produced. Some proteins are enzymes; the enzymes produced determine which reactions can occur. Those reactions determine cell activity.
The nuclear envelope separates the nucleus from the cytoplasm.
It contains nuclear pores.
Nuclear pores regulate passage of substances, including mRNA.
Chromosomes contain DNA wrapped around proteins called histones.
The DNA contains genes that code for proteins.
We’ll look at chromosome structure in greater detail in the Genes, Chromosomes & DNA section.
Mitochondria have a double membrane.
Mitochondria are the site of most stages of aerobic respiration.
Mitochondria transfer energy into ATP.
Muscle cells and sperm cells contain many mitochondria to supply ATP for contraction or movement.

nodes: Many mitochondria in muscle and sperm cells

blocks.html: Mitochondria transfer energy into ATP; they do not “make energy”.
The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is a membrane network of channels and flattened sacs.
The flattened membrane sacs are named cisternae.
Ribosomes are the site of translation.
Ribosomes join amino acids into polypeptides.
Ribosomes are found free in the cytoplasm or attached to rough ER.
Ribosomes can be attached to rough ER. This is one of the two locations described for ribosomes.
Rough ER has ribosomes attached to its surface.
Rough ER folds/processes proteins for secretion or membranes.
Rough ER transports proteins in vesicles.

links: are transported by rough ER in

blocks.html: The ER is connected to the nuclear envelope.
Rough ER is involved in protein synthesis, modification and transport.
Smooth ER has no ribosomes attached. Its lack of ribosomes distinguishes it from rough ER.

blocks.heading: Key point here
cells: Folds/processes proteins for secretion or membranes; transports them in vesicles

blocks.html: Smooth ER is involved in lipid synthesis.
Smooth ER is involved in detoxification.
Smooth ER is involved in Ca²⁺ storage.
The ER is a site of protein and lipid synthesis.
Ribosomes make polypeptides; ER processes and transports certain proteins.
Amino acids attach to tRNA in the cytoplasm, not specifically in ER.
The next questions practise recognition using the diagrams in this lesson. They do not assess identification in real microscope images.
The final check brings together structure recognition and the functions of the six specified structures.
First-attempt results and later corrections are recorded separately. Diagram questions remain separate from real-micrograph identification.

questions.title: Nucleus and cell activity
questions.prompt: Which relationship explains how protein production affects cell activity?
options: The enzymes produced determine which chemical reactions can occur.
The cell membrane produces the genes that code for proteins.
Ribosomes contain the chromosomes that control cell activities.
Mitochondria control which genes are switched on.
questions.feedback: Some proteins are enzymes. Which enzymes are produced determines which chemical reactions can occur, and these reactions determine cell activity.
